Stage 01

Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO transparency, Apostille authentication chain, official name clearance restricted wordlist, and pre-incorporation statutory fee budget.

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo (arts. 3, 4, 6, 14, 31 y 37), as amended by Ley 11/2018, de 28 de diciembre; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, por el que se aprueba el Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010 (arts. 3-10 y 39-40); Orden JUS/319/2018, de 6 de marzo, por la que se crea el Registro de Titularidades Reales de la Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado; Ley 39/2015, de 1 de octubre, del Procedimiento Administrativo Común de las Administraciones Públicas.
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A virtual office address is permissible solely for the initial commercial registry registration provided it corresponds to a physical postal address in Spain where official notifications may lawfully be served (arts. 9 and 10 Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010). However, for this specific venture capital general partner entity, a pure virtual mailbox without physical management premises, personnel, and documentary substance fails the CNMV's fit-and-proper and effective-board test and will lead to refusal or revocation of the SGEIC/GP license; SEPBLAC likewise requires the implementation of AML procedures and records at a physical establishment. The registered office must be adapted to a genuine operational office in Madrid, Barcelona, or Valencia before the CNMV license application is submitted.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

90 days

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

The relevant Provincial Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Provincial) for the company's registered office, coordinated through the Central Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil Central).

Governing statute

Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), principally Articles 4, 4 bis, 19-23, 30-35, 159-197, 210-241 and 272-279. If the entity manages venture capital or other closed-ended investment vehicles, Law 22/2014, including its authorization, capital, governance, conduct and reporting provisions for sociedades gestoras de entidades de inversión colectiva de tipo cerrado, also applies.

Formation / constitutional filings

Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), including the articles of association, filed electronically with the relevant Provincial Commercial Registry. The company acquires legal personality upon registration.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 163 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada may be incorporated with minimum share capital of EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. No statutory escrow account is required, although a bank certificate evidencing cash contribution is commonly obtained. If capital is below EUR 3,000, statutory reserve and creditor-protection rules apply until the prescribed threshold is reached. Any additional capital or own-funds requirement applicable to an SGEIC or regulated investment manager is separate and may be materially higher.

Funding & unlock path: Obtain the applicable municipal opening/activity clearance or responsible declaration, fire-protection design and certificate under Royal Decree 513/2017, and building and occupancy compliance under the Technical Building Code. Electrical, emergency lighting, HVAC and other regulated installations require authorized installer certificates and periodic inspection where applicable. Conduct workplace risk assessment, emergency planning, worker information and training under Law 31/1995 and its implementing regulations. Structural-load inspection is required where works, equipment or occupancy changes affect the building; it is not ordinarily a separate licensing condition for a standard office.

Paid-in capital rule: A Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada may be incorporated with minimum share capital of EUR 1. Capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. No statutory escrow account is required, although a bank certificate evidencing cash contribution is commonly obtained. If capital is below EUR 3,000, statutory reserve and creditor-protection rules apply until the prescribed threshold is reached. Any additional capital or own-funds requirement applicable to an SGEIC or regulated investment manager is separate and may be materially higher.

Pro-Forma First Board Resolution Draft
The Board resolves that: (1) the shares subscribed by the incorporators are confirmed as fully subscribed and paid in accordance with the incorporation deed; (2) the registered office at [full Spanish address] is adopted; (3) [name] is appointed Sole Director, or the persons listed in Schedule 1 are appointed directors, each accepting office and declaring no legal disqualification; (4) [name] is appointed attorney for tax, registry, banking and licensing filings; and (5) management shall obtain the company tax identification number, open the corporate bank account, maintain statutory books and implement applicable AML, regulatory and accounting controls.
Industrial Access / EIA & Civil Defense Approval Mandatory Environmental Clearance

National Securities Market Commission (CNMV) for regulated venture-capital management authorization; the competent autonomous-community industrial authority and municipality for premises, installations and activity controls. A pure office-based investment manager normally has no manufacturing licence.

Category: Authorization as a Sociedad Gestora de Entidades de Inversión Colectiva de Tipo Cerrado (SGEIC), under Law 22/2014, where the entity manages venture-capital entities or other qualifying closed-ended investment vehicles. A separate municipal opening/activity licence or responsible declaration may be required for the premises.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — Sede Electrónica: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es. Provincial/regional AEAT offices handle NIF certification, census filings, and VAT registration.

E-government filing portal

Foreign founders and administrators must first obtain an NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero). Prior to notarising the incorporation deed, request a provisional corporate NIF (CIF) from AEAT by filing Form 036; include the provisional CIF in the incorporation deed. Following registration of the deed in the Registro Mercantil (within 2 months), file the definitive declaración censal (Form 036) to confirm the definitive NIF (initial letter 'B' for an SL), disclose commencement of activity, the applicable IAE economic-activity epigraph for financial/venture-capital management services, and register for VAT (alta en IVA). Appoint a tax representative where required; obtain a Spanish digital certificate (FNMT/Cl@ve) for mandatory electronic filing of all tax returns.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — The SL is a resident corporate taxpayer subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Ley 27/2014) on worldwide income at 25%; newly created entities may apply a reduced 15% rate for the first two fiscal years of economic activity under art. 29.3 LIS. No pass-through or transparent treatment is available under general Spanish tax law. — Foreign founders and administrators must first obtain an NIE (Número de Identidad de Extranjero). Prior to notarising the incorporation deed, request a provisional corporate NIF (CIF) from AEAT by filing Form 036; include the provisional CIF in the incorporation deed. Following registration of the deed in the Registro Mercantil (within 2 months), file the definitive declaración censal (Form 036) to confirm the definitive NIF (initial letter 'B' for an SL), disclose commencement of activity, the applicable IAE economic-activity epigraph for financial/venture-capital management services, and register for VAT (alta en IVA). Appoint a tax representative where required; obtain a Spanish digital certificate (FNMT/Cl@ve) for mandatory electronic filing of all tax returns.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation — The SL is a resident corporate taxpayer subject to Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Ley 27/2014) on worldwide income at 25%; newly created entities may apply a reduced 15% rate for the first two fiscal years of economic activity under art. 29.3 LIS. No pass-through or transparent treatment is available under general Spanish tax law.

Available election forms

Spain does not administer a check-the-box or elective pass-through classification; legal form determines taxation. Statutory elections relevant to a venture-capital GP entity include: (i) the 15% new-entity CIT rate (art. 29.3 LIS); (ii) fiscal consolidation group election under art. 61 LIS where the GP is owned ≥75% by a resident entity; (iii) application of the 95% participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains under art. 21 LIS, subject to the 5% minimum shareholding and one-year holding period; (iv) capitalisation and levelling reserves under arts. 25–26 LIS; (v) VAT elections, including the monthly refund scheme (REDEME), SII opt-in, and intra-community operator registration; (vi) no optional hybrid-mismatch election — ATAD anti-hybrid rules under art. 15 bis LGT apply mandatorily.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No annual turnover registration threshold applies to established Spanish entities — Spanish VAT registration is mandatory from the first euro of taxable economic activity. Non-EU suppliers without a Spanish establishment must register from the first transaction and appoint a VAT representative; EU suppliers of distance sales and electronically supplied services apply the pan-EU €10,000 annual threshold under art. 70.ter.3 LIVA.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Goods: art. 21.1 LIVA zero-rates exports where goods physically leave EU territory, typically within 90 days of dispatch, and the exporter substantiates departure through a Customs Export Declaration (DUA) issued in its own name plus transport documentation; intra-EU supplies are exempt (not zero-rated) under art. 25 LIVA with the customer's EU VAT ID declared in VIES. Services: venture-capital management and advisory services provided to non-EU funds or non-EU investors fall outside the scope of Spanish VAT under art. 69.1.1º LIVA (B2B place-of-supply rule) where the recipient is established outside Spain and has no Spanish permanent establishment; however, management services invoiced to Spanish-resident fund investors or funds attract standard IVA at 21%, and the art. 20.1.18º LIVA exemption does not extend to the management of venture-capital/ECR funds.

  • Customs Export Declaration (DUA — Documento Único Administrativo) validated by Spanish customs, with exporter identification, HS code, value, and exit-office stamp.
  • Transport document — Bill of Lading, CMR/CIM, or House/Master Air Waybill — evidencing physical departure of the goods from EU territory to the non-EU destination, consistent with DUA and commercial invoice data.
  • Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Ingreso de Divisas) or equivalent bank/SWIFT credit confirmation showing the export consideration credited to the SL's resident account in the invoiced currency.
  • Commercial invoice, packing list, EUR.1/ATR certificate (where preferential origin is claimed), and any applicable export licence or controlled-technology declaration.
  • For offshore services: executed management/investment-advisory agreement identifying the non-EU recipient, the recipient's foreign VAT/TIN reference, wiring/payment instructions, and documentary evidence that the recipient lacks a Spanish permanent establishment.

SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) under Reglamento 596/2016 imposes real-time VAT book-record reporting to AEAT via XML web services (within 8 days, or 4 days for monthly filers) for taxpayers with invoiced turnover exceeding €6,000,000 per annum and myself VAT-group members. Separately, Ley Crea y Crece (Law 18/2022) and Royal Decree 1007/2023 (VeriFactu) mandate B2B electronic invoicing for all companies, requiring an integrity-protected XML/QR hash stamp; transmission to AEAT or to an accredited private invoicing platform must occur in real time or within 4 calendar days, effectively creating a digital fiscal clearance and stamping procedure.

AEAT cross-matches customs exit data, bank SWIFT receipts, SII records, and VIES statements to identify improper zero-rating. Upon detection, AEAT recharacterises the supply and assesses VAT at 21% on the original consideration, plus statutory late-payment interest (interés de demora). Voluntary late correction attracts escalating 1%-per-month surcharges up to 20% (art. 27 LGT); audited assessments and concealment trigger sanctions of 50%–150% of the under-declared tax (art. 191 LGT), with aggravated penalties for false invoices under art. 201 LGT, clawback of refunded input VAT, exclusion from REDEME/SII privileges, and criminal liability under art. 305 Código Penal (imprisonment of 1–5 years and fines up to six times the defrauded amount) where the annual defrauded quota exceeds €120,000.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

Spain uses the euro and has no general exchange controls between euro-area jurisdictions. Current-account payments, including management fees, dividends, interest, trade payments and ordinary service payments, are generally freely transferable, subject to anti-money-laundering, sanctions, tax and financial-sector rules. Capital-account transactions, including shareholder funding, intercompany loans, acquisitions, fund commitments and distributions, are generally permitted but may trigger statistical, foreign-investment, tax, beneficial-ownership or sectoral reporting. Profit remittance normally requires distributable accounting profits, approval of annual accounts and distributions, maintenance of mandatory legal reserves, satisfaction of creditor-protection rules, applicable withholding-tax analysis and evidence of the underlying transaction. A venture-capital general partner or manager may require authorization or registration with the Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores under Law 22/2014 and applicable AIFMD rules; banking access does not replace that regulatory requirement. Transfers involving sanctioned parties, high-risk jurisdictions, opaque ownership, unexplained third-party funding or unlicensed fund-raising may be blocked or escalated by the bank.

Export proceeds surrender rules

Spain has no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to the central bank, no general mandatory conversion ratio and no universal statutory conversion deadline for ordinary export receipts. Export proceeds may generally remain in euros or another permitted currency and may be held with an authorized bank, subject to contractual banking terms and accounting, tax and statistical reporting. Payment-service providers and financial institutions perform transaction and balance-of-payments reporting under applicable Spanish and European rules; direct external financial transactions may require resident reporting where a prescribed form, threshold or category applies. For this entity, the expected revenue is primarily management fees, carried interest and investment-related services rather than merchandise exports; each receipt should be classified using the bank's purpose code and supported by the management agreement, invoice, fund documentation and tax records.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank monetary and foreign-exchange framework. Spain's foreign-exchange reporting and investment-control framework is supplemented by the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Enterprise and the State Tax Administration Agency where applicable.

Annual Statutory Maintenance

Statutory filing calendar, progressive late penalties, external audit triggers, and statutory registers.

Statutory Filing Calendar

Statutory deliverableDeadline window Government feeDelinquency sanctions
Annual Deposit of Statutory Financial Statements (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales): balance sheet, profit and loss account, notes, management report, audit report, and beneficial-ownership box (casilla 609) Shareholders' meeting must approve the annual accounts within 6 months after fiscal year-end (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end); deposit with the Commercial Registry within 1 month after approval, i.e., no later than 31 July for calendar-year companies; anniversary rule applies to off-calendar fiscal years $0 USD Late or non-deposit triggers cierre registral from the deposit deadline onward, blocking all subsequent corporate registrations (administrative strike-off equivalent); graduated administrative fine of EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000 under Article 283.1 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital; two consecutive years of non-deposit allow coercive dissolution proceedings; defective UBO information is additionally sanctioned under AML Law 10/2010
Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Modelo 200) Due on the 25th day of the 6th month following the end of the tax period; for calendar-year SLs the hard deadline is 25 July; off-calendar taxpayers follow the 6-month-plus-25-day anniversary rule $0 USD Late filing without prior demand triggers the sliding recargo of 5%, 10%, 15% or 20% of the amount due plus late-payment interest accruing from 26 July; additional flat and proportional penalties under Article 198 LGT up to 100% of omitted tax; intentional concealment above 25% of declared tax basis may trigger criminal referral under Article 305 of the Penal Code
Annual Value-Added Tax Recapitulative Declaration (Declaración-Resumen Anual de IVA, Modelo 390) By 30 January following the calendar year in which VAT accrued; for non-calendar-year VAT periods, within 30 days after the close of the annual VAT period $0 USD Late filing triggers recargo of 5% to 20% of the VAT due plus late-payment interest; Article 198 LGT proportional penalties apply to omitted annual VAT data; access to VAT refund requests and monthly offsetting modalities is suspended until the annual recap is presented
Annual Summary of Withholding Tax Payments on Employment and Professional Income (Resumen Anual de Retenciones e Ingresos a Cuenta, Modelo 190) By 31 January following the calendar year in which salaries, director fees, and professional service remunerations were paid and withheld; zero-filing is mandatory when the SL has withholding obligations even if no amounts were accrued $0 USD Article 198 LGT penalties apply: EUR 200 flat fine for economically relevant information and proportional penalties of 2% to 20% on unreported withholding bases; repeated late filing can raise the flat fine to EUR 20,000; untimely presentation delays refund of excess withholdings and blocks issuance of creditor tax-residence certificates
Annual Related-Party Transaction Informative Return (Declaración de Operaciones Vinculadas, Modelo 232) Filed during the month of November following the tax year (1–30 November); for a 31 December fiscal year-end, the return is due in November of the following year $0 USD Article 198 LGT imposes a proportional penalty of 1% of the net amount of omitted related-party transactions when the data are not reported, subject to minima and maxima of EUR 300 and EUR 20,000 per year; failure to file also weakens transfer-pricing documentation and may trigger adjustment plus 20% penalty under Article 130 LGT
Annual return deadline

Shareholders' meeting must approve the annual accounts within 6 months after fiscal year-end (by 30 June for a 31 December year-end); deposit with the Commercial Registry within 1 month after approval, i.e., no later than 31 July for calendar-year companies; anniversary rule applies to off-calendar fiscal years

Statutory government annual fee

$0 USD

Late filing penalties

Late or non-deposit triggers cierre registral from the deposit deadline onward, blocking all subsequent corporate registrations (administrative strike-off equivalent); graduated administrative fine of EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000 under Article 283.1 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital; two consecutive years of non-deposit allow coercive dissolution proceedings; defective UBO information is additionally sanctioned under AML Law 10/2010

BoxField Non-resident guidanceTax-evasion pitfall

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

Master / Local File threshold: €20,000,000 consolidated annual revenue

Economic substance scope: Mandatory under Law 11/2018 and OECD ESR for high-risk activities including venture capital fund management; requires adequate employees, premises, and core income-generating activities in Spain

Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

Tax Evasion

Statutory sanction: Criminal penalties: fines up to five times evaded tax, imprisonment up to five years

Director personal liability: Personal criminal liability; disqualification from management, fines, and imprisonment
Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure

Statutory sanction: Administrative fines €1,500 to €300,000 or higher

Director personal liability: Joint and several liability for penalties; potential criminal liability if intentional
Economic Substance and Shell Company Violation

Statutory sanction: Revocation of registration, fines up to €1 million, criminal prosecution

Director personal liability: Piercing of corporate veil; civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment for fraud
AML and Tax Fraud

Statutory sanction: Fines €100,000 to €5 million or more; criminal sanctions

Director personal liability: Personal liability including disqualification, fines, and possible imprisonment
